title: Locker and Detention
premise: Kestrel Ashgrove has spent four years at Hollowmere Academy keeping his head down, but when the school's ghost — the legendary 'Warden' who supposedly died in a 1970s fire — starts leaving notes in his locker addressed to him in ink that shouldn't exist, he's pulled into a mystery the board buried decades ago: students who 'transferred out' and never existed. Following the notes, Kestrel uncovers that his own scholarship is part of a quiet pattern of erasing students the school found inconvenient, and that the Warden was one of them. At the final game of the season, Kestrel exposes the board's records publicly, forcing the academy to acknowledge its erased students — and discovering the Warden's true identity is someone far closer to him than he ever imagined.
about_author: Paloma Oyelaran is a former boarding school librarian who spent years cataloguing the marginalia students left in old textbooks, an obsession that fuels her fiction. She writes stories about quiet kids who discover the institutions around them are louder and stranger than they seem.

chapters.title: The Counting Days
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Establishes his invisibility at Hollowmere: scholarship kid, cafeteria margins, a countdown app to graduation. He survives by being unremarkable. Emotional beat: weary resignation, the ache of belonging nowhere.

chapters.title: Ink That Shouldn't Be
chapters.summary: Kestrel finds the first note in his locker — his full name, written in ink that shimmers wet but never dries. No one claims it. His roommate Dex jokes it's a prank; Kestrel feels seen in a way that terrifies him. Beat: unease laced with forbidden thrill.

chapters.title: The Warden's Legend
chapters.summary: Kestrel researches the school ghost in the library archives, where he meets Marisol, a fellow scholarship student who knows the Warden legend: a student who died in the 1974 fire. First real friendship sparks. Beat: tentative connection.

chapters.title: A Second Note
chapters.summary: A new note predicts an event before it happens — the gym flood. Kestrel watches it come true. Marisol believes him; Dex grows oddly evasive about his own scholarship paperwork. Beat: dread replacing curiosity.

chapters.title: Transferred Out
chapters.summary: Kestrel finds the Warden's student file: no forwarding records, no family listed, marked 'transferred' though the fire killed her. He notices three other names with the same stamp across decades. Beat: the first crack of real conspiracy.

chapters.title: Detention with Mr. Voss
chapters.summary: Kestrel is caught in the archives and assigned detention with Mr. Voss, the board's loyal dean of students, who warns him about 'obsessions.' Kestrel notices Voss keeps a key ring with a locker key from a demolished wing. Beat: watched, cornered, defiant.

chapters.title: Marisol's Ledger
chapters.summary: Marisol reveals she's been tracking scholarship students who left mid-year for years — all 'transferred,' all untraceable, all kids with no money and no advocates. Kestrel realizes he fits the profile. Beat: cold recognition, fear of being next.

chapters.title: The Demolished Wing
chapters.summary: Kestrel uses the stolen key to enter the sealed east wing: scorched lockers, and one — locker 114 — that's warm to the touch. Inside, a fresh note: 'They'll do to you what they did to me.' Beat: the ghost is real, and it's protecting him.

chapters.title: What Dex Knows
chapters.summary: Kestrel confronts Dex, whose father sits on the board. Dex admits he was placed at Hollowmere to watch scholarship students and report 'instability.' Their friendship fractures. Beat: betrayal, and pity — Dex is a prisoner too.

chapters.title: Midterm Warning
chapters.summary: A note warns Kestrel that the board meets after midterms to 'review the current cohort.' Marisol's name appears on a review list. Kestrel must choose: stay invisible or act. Beat: the cost of caring.

chapters.title: Breaking Into Records
chapters.summary: Kestrel and Marisol infiltrate the administration building at night, photographing decades of erased students. Voss nearly catches them; Marisol's scraped knee blood on the floor becomes a clue Voss uses to hunt them. Beat: exhilaration curdling into hunted panic.

chapters.title: The Photograph
chapters.summary: Among the records, Kestrel finds a 1974 photo: the Warden, alive, standing beside a young teacher — who looks exactly like the school's ancient groundskeeper, Mr. Ellery. Beat: the past is not past; someone survived and stayed.

chapters.title: Ellery's Confession
chapters.summary: Mr. Ellery admits he was the Warden's teacher and boyfriend; the fire was set to destroy records of a scholarship fraud scheme, and the students who knew were 'transferred' — disappeared into the system. He never learned what happened to her. Beat: grief across fifty years.

chapters.title: Locker 114
chapters.summary: Kestrel opens locker 114 fully and finds the Warden's journal, its pages still writing themselves. Her name: Adaeze Okafor. The notes have been her, anchored to the school by the injustice. Beat: the ghost becomes a person; Kestrel sees himself in her.

chapters.title: Suspension Papers
chapters.summary: Voss moves to expel Kestrel on fabricated grounds before the board meeting. Dex, guilt-ridden, tips them off and hands over board meeting minutes proving the 'review cohort' practice never ended. Beat: an unlikely ally crosses the line.

chapters.title: The Last Game Approaches
chapters.summary: The board plans to announce a new 'merit restructuring' at the championship game — cover for erasing this year's scholarship cohort. Kestrel, Marisol, and Dex have until Friday to act. Beat: ticking clock, resolve hardening.

chapters.title: What Adaeze Wants
chapters.summary: The journal reveals Adaeze doesn't want revenge — she wants her name read aloud at the school that erased it, and the others' names with it. Kestrel realizes exposure isn't enough; there must be remembrance. Beat: the mission gains its soul.

chapters.title: Voss Closes In
chapters.summary: Voss searches dorms, seizes Marisol's ledger, and threatens her scholarship. Kestrel must decide whether to run the plan without her or delay and lose the window. He chooses to carry both their parts. Beat: sacrifice, loneliness before the end.

chapters.title: The Final Game
chapters.summary: Climax. During the championship's halftime, Kestrel takes the microphone, reads the erased students' names, and broadcasts the records over the stadium screens as Adaeze's ink blazes across the scoreboard. The crowd, the press, the board — all witness. Beat: triumphant, terrifying exposure.

chapters.title: After the Whistle
chapters.summary: The board scrambles; Voss resigns; an independent inquiry begins. Hollowmere must reckon publicly. Kestrel faces expulsion but the alumni and press pressure makes the board back down. Beat: fragile, hard-won vindication.

chapters.title: The Names Read Aloud
chapters.summary: At a memorial assembly, Kestrel reads all forty-one erased names, ending with Adaeze Okafor. The ink notes stop. Locker 114 goes cold. Kestrel grieves the friend he never met. Beat: mourning and peace entwined.

chapters.title: Graduation Day
chapters.summary: Kestrel deletes the countdown app. He, Marisol, and Dex — changed — walk at graduation, and Kestrel finds one last note in his locker: 'Thank you for staying visible.' He keeps it. Beat: belonging, finally, on his own terms.
